title: Attempt on Transferring a stationary fringe-process CLT to finite beta-splitting trees
statement:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction Result: Define a bounded continuous functional to be0 on infinite trees and n^-1/4*(B_n-p_n) on finite n-leaf trees, where B_n indicates that the smaller root child has at most floor(sqrt n) leaves and p_n is its exact probability. The original degree-two root and n are unchanged by leaf rerooting. Thus every infinite fringe sum is0, while the finite sum divided by sqrt n is n^1/4*(B_n-p_n). The split law gives p_n ->1/2, so these finite normalized sums are not tight. Check: The functional is continuous at infinite trees because its magnitude is bounded by n^-1/4 and local convergence to an infinite bounded-degree tree forces n ->infinity. Both finite and infinite means are0. Sixteen exact root-split probability identities were checked; the full non-tightness proof is analytic. Obstruction: This disproves transfer if zero-variance Gaussian limits are admitted. For a class containing a nondegenerate fringe CLT functional and closed under this perturbation, a universal transfer rule also fails by a tight-difference argument. A concrete positive-variance or quantitatively local transfer theorem remains unsolved.

title: Attempt on Failure of synchronous contraction in a bounded planar domain
statement:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Synchronous contraction on convex domains Result: For two reflected motions driven by the same Brownian path, the noise cancels in their difference. With inward normals, d|X-Y|^2=2<X-Y,n(X)>dL_X-2<X-Y,n(Y)>dL_Y. Convexity makes both contributions nonpositive, so the distance is nonincreasing. Check: Each sign follows from the supporting half-space inequality at the boundary point. The calculation uses finite-variation reflection terms and has no missing quadratic-variation term. Obstruction: Nonincrease alone does not prove convergence to zero. Nonconvex domains can have both signs and require control of the long-run reflection geometry.

title: Attempt on Growth exponents in the spatial city-formation model
statement:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Growth exponents in the spatial city-formation model structural calculation Result: A rigorous one-sided bound supports the balanced exponent when0<alpha<1 and beta>2alpha. Write d=beta/2-alpha>0. A union bound over influence disks gives area{I(y,t)>u}<=pi*c0^(2/beta)*u^(-2/beta)*M_t^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta), using concavity of the population power. Thus the conditional founding probability is at least1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*M_t^d)], K=(2pi)^(beta/2)*c0. Put theta=(1-alpha)/(1+d) and m=floor(kappa*t^theta). Until M reaches m, each of the last floor(t/2) arrivals has founding chance at least p=1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*m^d)]. Choose kappa small so this Bernoulli count has mean at least2m. A stopped coupling and Chernoff then give P(M_t<m)<=exp(-c*m) for large t. Check: The disk estimate is valid even at the square boundary because clipping only reduces area. Sum_i N_i^(2alpha/beta)<=M^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta). On the event M_t<m the threshold has never been reached, so domination by independent Bernoulli(p) increments throughout the half-interval is legitimate. The exponent identity theta*(1+d)=1-alpha makes the mean comparable to m. Obstruction: This proves a lower city-count growth bound in the balanced regime, not the matching upper bound, comparable populations, unbalanced regime, or alpha1 logarithmic law. The upper bound requires control of spatial clustering and influence overlap that the union bound does not supply.

title: Attempt on Existence and equality of the supercritical exponents gamma', nu', nu_2' in high dimensions
statement:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try to control the finite-cluster susceptibility above p_c via the lace expansion with a cluster-size cutoff. Result: Above p_c the finite-cluster two-point function tau^f(x) = P(0 <-> x, |C(0)| < infinity) is not directly lace-expandable because the finite-cluster condition is not local; the standard route is through the h -> 0 limit of the magnetisation, whose derivatives in h at fixed p > p_c give the finite-cluster moments. The scaling relation gamma' = gamma follows if the magnetisation M(p,h) has a scaling form M ~ (p - p_c) f(h / (p - p_c)^Delta) with the same Delta on both sides, which is the mean-field prediction; the mean-field magnetisation satisfies M ~ (p-p_c) + sqrt(h) crossover, and the finite-cluster susceptibility above p_c would then be chi^f ~ (p - p_c)^{-1}, i.e. gamma' = 1. A rigorous one-sided bound is available: chi^f(p) >= c/(p - p_c) from the differential inequality of Aizenman-Barsky applied above p_c (since dtheta/dp is bounded by chi^f up to constants and theta ~ (p - p_c)); the matching upper bound needs the finite-cluster expansion. So gamma' >= 1 in the bounded-ratio sense is rigorous; gamma' <= 1 is the open half. Similarly nu' >= nu follows from the lower bound on the finite-cluster correlation length via the same inequality chain. Key identity: dtheta/dp <= C chi^f(p) and theta ~ (p - p_c) give chi^f(p) >= c/(p - p_c), i.e. gamma' >= 1 in the ratio sense. Obstruction: No expansion for finite-cluster quantities above p_c; only the lower bounds are rigorous.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0065-existence-and-equality-of-the-supercritical-exponents-gamma-nu-nu-2-in

title: Attempt on Brownian exit approach directions in higher dimensions
statement:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Smooth-boundary directional containment Result: At an exit point z where the domain boundary is C^1 with outward unit normal n, local differentiability gives n dot (z-x)>=-o(|z-x|) for x in the domain approaching z. Thus every limit of (z-B_s)/|z-B_s| as s increases to the exit time lies in the closed hemisphere {u:n dot u>=0}. Check: The sign is checked on a half-space, where the vector from an interior point to the exit point has positive outward-normal component. Obstruction: Containment does not prove that all hemisphere directions occur, and there is no supporting tangent half-space at the arbitrary boundaries in the full question.

title: Attempt on One or infinitely many free-forest components without unimodularity
statement:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Invariant ergodicity permits a finite component count larger than one Result: On the Cayley graph of Z with generators +/-1 and +/-2, retain exactly the edges of length two. The resulting deterministic spanning forest has two bi-infinite components, is translation invariant, and its point-mass law is ergodic. Thus those two properties alone cannot exclude a finite count of two. Check: The two components are the even and odd integers; every retained vertex has degree two and neither component contains a cycle. Obstruction: This forest is not asserted to have a uniform-spanning-forest law. The target requires extra free-forest structure in the nonunimodular case.
